title: Functional and clinical outcome of surgical gluteal tendon fixation
summary:
A large number of patients suffer from complaints of the hip, which can be accompanied by considerable restrictions in everyday life and a reduction in quality of life. Reasons for these complaints may be overloading of the tendon attachment of the lateral gluteal muscles, which is primarily responsible for spreading the leg and thus also for stabilization in the one-legged position. The disease, known as insertion tendinopathy (irritation of the insertion tendon), is characterized by inflammatory changes and a state of irritation of this tendon insertion, which can be associated with severe pain.
So-called suture anchors are used to reattach the gluteal muscles to the pelvis in case of (partial) rupture. These are connected to the musculature with tear-proof threads. The aim of this study is to investigate how surgical gluteal tendon refixation affects pain and function of the affected hip. Patients will be examined after 3 and 12 months. 
The aim of the study is to obtain an accurate description of the data of patients with gluteal tendon insufficiency. In addition, the success of surgery after surgical gluteal tendon refixation will be assessed, primarily on the basis of parameters describing pain and function of the affected hip joint. In addition, parameters from the blood (biomarkers) will be examined for a connection with tendon healing. A gait analysis and isokinetic force measurement are planned the day before surgery, these examinations will be repeated after 12 months.
A radiological check is performed according to routine or if clinically necessary.
Magnetic resonance imaging is required prior to surgery, but this is not part of the non-invasive study. After 12 months, a further MRI examination is planned for all patients who do not find this stressful. In addition, blood will be taken from the study participants before the operation within the recording routine. In addition, another small amount (approx. 10ml) will be taken to examine various serum parameters, which will be examined as biomarkers for a correlation with tendon healing.
conditions: Injury of muscle and tendon at hip and thigh level

interventions.name: Patients suffering from gluteal muscle rupture will be included in this study after diagnosis during an outpatient presentation at the clinic. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-indication for isolated gluteal tendon refixation without accompanying additional surgical measures in the hip joint area
-patient age ≥ 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
-Symptomatic accompanying pathologies of the hip joint to be treated
-symptomatic, but radiologically significant degenerative, congenital or surgically induced changes in the hip joint to be treated (e.g. coxarthrosis grade 3 or higher according to Kellgren and Lawrence, higher grade hip dysplasia with CE angle <20°, after osteotomy or endoprosthetic treatment)
-accompanying diseases that have an influence on the gait pattern
-obesity, which makes it impossible to carry out a valid gait analysis (guideline value BMI <30-35, depending on fat distribution pattern).
